args.body:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
MEMORANDUM TO THE TRELLIS BIOWORKS SPECIAL COMMITTEE
PROJECT LATTICE — ESCALATION MEMORANDUM REGARDING HALBERD HOLDINGS SECOND-TURN MARKUP OF SPA ARTICLE VIII (INDEMNIFICATION)

From: Trellis BioWorks Deal Team, Project Lattice
Re: Halberd Holdings LP second-turn markup of SPA Article VIII vs. execution draft v4, and requests exceeding deal team delegated authority
Reference Purchase Price: $120,000,000 (SPA Article I, subject to Section 2.4 adjustments)

This memorandum compares each change in Wexler Bright LLP's second-turn markup of Article VIII (transmitted 30 July 2026 against our execution draft v4) against (i) the v4 sell-side position and (ii) the deal team's approved fallback positions (memorandum approved by the Transaction Committee 24 July 2026). It quantifies cap and basket deltas in dollars, identifies which asks exceed the deal team's delegated authority, addresses the proposed special indemnity by reference to the specific disclosed Schedule 3.14 items it would cover, and closes with a recommendation and approval request.

Per the deal team's approved logistics (IP-5), all work product is filed in the Trellis matter workspace under Trellis naming conventions only; we have not adopted Halberd's proposed counterparty filename (halberd-special-indemnity-schedule.docx), data-room mirroring request, or transmittal logistics for our internal workspace.

SECTION-BY-SECTION ANALYSIS

1. SECTION 8.1 (SURVIVAL — GENERAL REPRESENTATIONS)
- v4 position: general representations survive eighteen (18) months.
- Halberd ask: thirty-six (36) months. Fundamental Representations and tax survival unchanged.
- Deal team approved fallback (IP-1): opening 18 months; approved fallback maximum twenty-four (24) months. A 36-month survival period is expressly out of policy.
- Assessment: The Halberd ask of 36 months EXCEEDS the deal team's delegated authority (24-month fallback ceiling by 12 months).

2. SECTION 8.3(a) (BASKET / DEDUCTIBLE)
- v4 position: true deductible of $400,000, with recovery only of the excess above the Deductible.
- Halberd ask: convert to a tipping basket of $250,000 — once aggregate Losses exceed $250,000, the Sellers are liable from the first dollar.
- Deal team approved fallback (IP-3): the basket must remain a true deductible; conversion to a tipping basket is out of policy at any threshold; the deductible may be reduced from $400,000 but not below a floor of $300,000.
- Assessment: Two independent deviations. (a) Structural — Halberd seeks to convert a true deductible to a tipping basket, which is out of policy at any threshold; this structure itself EXCEEDS delegated authority regardless of dollar amount. (b) Threshold — even if a true deductible were retained, Halberd's $250,000 level would breach the deal team's $300,000 floor by $50,000. In dollar terms against the $120,000,000 Purchase Price, the v4 true-deductible position (leveraging $400,000, excess-only) versus a permitted floor of $300,000 represents up to $100,000 of incremental first-dollar exposure; Halberd's structure would eliminate the excess-only mechanic entirely from the first dollar above $250,000, exposing the full quantum of any covered Losses in excess of $250,000. This ask EXCEEDS delegated authority.

3. SECTION 8.3(b) (CAP)
- v4 position: aggregate cap of ten percent (10%) of the Purchase Price = $12,000,000. Fundamental Representations capped at the Purchase Price.
- Halberd ask: twenty-five percent (25%) of the Purchase Price = $30,000,000. Fundamental Representations remain capped at the Purchase Price.
- Deal team approved fallback (IP-2): opening 10% ($12,000,000); approved fallback maximum fifteen percent (15%) = $18,000,000. A 25% cap is out of policy.
- Cap Delta (in dollars): 
  • vs. v4 ($12,000,000): Halberd's $30,000,000 represents a $18,000,000 increase in aggregate seller liability.
  • vs. deal team fallback ($18,000,000): Halberd's ask exceeds the fallback by $12,000,000.
- Assessment: This ask EXCEEDS the deal team's delegated authority (25% vs. 15% fallback ceiling; $18,000,000 delta from v4, $12,000,000 beyond the fallback).

4. NEW SECTION 8.2(d) (SPECIAL INDEMNITY FOR DISCLOSED MATTERS) — WITH REFERENCE TO DISCLOSURE SCHEDULE 3.14
- v4 position: execution draft v4 contains no special indemnities.
- Halberd ask: the Sellers shall indemnify Buyer for any and all Losses arising out of or relating to the matters disclosed on Schedule 3.14, which indemnity shall NOT be subject to the Deductible or the cap in Section 8.3, and shall survive until the expiration of the applicable statutes of limitation. This is an uncapped special indemnity with unlimited survival, free of the Deductible and cap.
- Deal team approved fallback (IP-4): a special indemnity for disclosed matters is acceptable only if all of the following hold: (i) scope limited to Schedule 3.14 Item 1 and Item 2 (the pending matters); (ii) aggregate cap of $2,500,000; (iii) survival of twenty-four (24) months from Closing; and (iv) resolved matters — including Schedule 3.14 Item 3 — expressly excluded. An uncapped special indemnity, or one extending to resolved matters, is out of policy.

Scope of Schedule 3.14 items the Halberd special indemnity would cover:
- Schedule 3.14 Item 1 (TRELLIGEN trademark opposition) — TTAB Opposition No. 91-284772, Lumenor Devices B.V. v. Trellis BioWorks, Inc., filed 11 February 2026; pending; discovery conference held 5 May 2026. No damages claimed; exposure is potential refusal of registration and associated rebranding of the TRELLIGEN assay line. The Company continues use at common law. (Pending matter — within the deal team's acceptable Item 1/Item 2 scope, but the Halberd pricing violates the deal team parameters.)
- Schedule 3.14 Item 2 (Bexley Clinical Partners customer dispute) — written demand of 3 April 2026 claiming $1,850,000 in damages for alleged assay lot failures under the 2024 Supply Agreement; pending, pre-litigation; Company denied liability 24 April 2026; carrier noticed 28 April 2026, coverage reserved. (Pending matter — within the deal team's acceptable Item 1/Item 2 scope, but the Halberd pricing violates the deal team parameters.)
- Schedule 3.14 Item 3 (OSHA citation) — Citation No. 1829445 (Region IV) issued 9 January 2026; resolved by informal settlement; penalty of $46,500 paid in full 17 March 2026; abatement certified 2 March 2026; disclosed as a resolved matter only. (Resolved matter — expressly required to be excluded under the deal team's IP-4 condition (iv); Halberd's blanket reference to "the matters disclosed on Schedule 3.14" would sweep in this resolved matter.)

Deviations from deal team IP-4 parameters (all four conditions breached):
(i) Scope — Halberd references all of "Schedule 3.14," not limited to Item 1 and Item 2; it would extend to resolved Item 3.
(ii) Cap — Halberd's ask is uncapped (no aggregate dollar limit), versus the deal team's approved cap of $2,500,000. There is no fixed dollar delta because the ask is unbounded; at minimum it represents an open-ended increase of at least $2,500,000 over the deal team's approved ceiling.
(iii) Survival — Halberd asks survival until the expiration of the applicable statutes of limitation, versus the deal team's approved 24-month survival; this is open-ended and materially longer (often several years or more) than 24 months.
(iv) Resolved matters exclusion — Halberd's blanket language fails to exclude Item 3, which IP-4 requires.
- Assessment: The Halberd special-indemnity request EXCEEDS the deal team's delegated authority on every dimension. It is uncapped, extends to resolved matters, and survives to the statute of limitations — all expressly out of policy.

5. SECTION 8.5 (ORDER OF RECOVERY — CONFORMING CHANGE)
- v4 position: Buyer shall recover first from the Escrow Amount and thereafter severally from the Sellers in proportion to their Pro Rata Shares.
- Halberd ask (conforming change): special-indemnity claims recoverable directly from the Sellers without first exhausting the Escrow Amount.
- Assessment: This is a conforming change that tracks the proposed Section 8.2(d) special indemnity. It is acceptable only if and to the extent the underlying special indemnity is brought within the deal team's IP-4 parameters; as presented (for an uncapped, unlimited-survival, all-Schedule-3.14 indemnity), it is a feature of the out-of-policy ask and does not independently grant authority.

SUMMARY OF ASKS EXCEEDING DEAL TEAM DELEGATED AUTHORITY
All four substantive asks in the Halberd second turn exceed the deal team's approved fallbacks:
1. Section 8.1 — 36-month general survival exceeds the 24-month fallback by 12 months.
2. Section 8.3(a) — tipping-basket structure (out of policy at any threshold) and $250,000 threshold below the $300,000 floor.
3. Section 8.3(b) — 25% cap ($30,000,000) exceeds the 15% fallback ($18,000,000) by $12,000,000, and $18,000,000 above the v4 10% cap.
4. New Section 8.2(d) — uncapped special indemnity over all of Schedule 3.14 (including resolved Item 3), surviving to the statute of limitations, and free of Deductible and cap; breaches all four IP-4 conditions.
5. Section 8.5 — conforming order-of-recovery change acceptable only if the special indemnity is conformed to IP-4.

QUANTIFICATION SUMMARY (against the $120,000,000 Purchase Price)
- Cap: v4 $12,000,000 (10%) → deal fallback $18,000,000 (15%) → Halberd ask $30,000,000 (25%). Halberd ask = $18,000,000 above v4 and $12,000,000 above the fallback.
- Basket: v4 true deductible $400,000 (excess-only) → deal floor $300,000 → Halberd tipping basket $250,000 (from first dollar). Halberd's structural change eliminates excess-only exposure above $250,000; its threshold is $50,000 below the deal floor and $150,000 below the v4 deductible.
- Special indemnity: uncapped (no finite dollar delta), versus deal approved cap of $2,500,000; open-ended survival versus 24-month fallback.

RECOMMENDATION AND APPROVAL REQUEST
Recommendation: The Trellis BioWorks Special Committee should reject the Halberd second-turn Article VIII markup in its current form. Each substantive ask exceeds the deal team's delegated authority, and the special indemnity as drafted is uncapped, extends to resolved Schedule 3.14 Item 3, and survives to statute-of-limitations — all directly contrary to the deal team's IP-4 parameters.

We recommend that the Special Committee authorize the deal team to respond on the following basis:
1. Survival: counter at the deal team's approved 24-month fallback (IP-1); do not accept 36 months.
2. Basket: retain a true deductible (out-of-policy for a tipping basket), and hold at or above the $300,000 deductible floor (IP-3).
3. Cap: counter at the deal team's approved 15% fallback ($18,000,000), with Fundamental Representations not to exceed the Purchase Price (IP-2); do not accept 25%.
4. Special indemnity: offer, if negotiated, a special indemnity strictly confined to Schedule 3.14 Item 1 and Item 2, capped at $2,500,000, surviving 24 months from Closing, and expressly excluding resolved matters (including Item 3), with the conforming Section 8.5 order-of-recovery change applying only on that conformed basis (IP-4).

Respectfully submitted for Special Committee approval. We request authorization to (a) reject the current markup and (b) respond within the approved fallback parameters set out above. Absent Special Committee approval, the deal team will make no further concessions beyond the approved fallbacks.

Trellis BioWorks Deal Team — Project Lattice
[Privileged and Confidential — Prepared in Anticipation of Litigation and Negotiations]
